recipes.name: Easy Corn Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 (11 ounce) can whole niblet style corn
1 (8.5 ounce) package dry corn bread mix

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease an 8 x12-inch casserole dish.
Combine cream corn, niblet corn, cornbread mix, sour cream, butter, and eggs, in a large bowl. Pour into the prepared casserole dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until lightly brown, about 30 minutes.
Sprinkle cheese over top; continue baking until center is firm, about 15 minutes more.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Corn Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This easy corn casserole recipe combines sweet creamed, niblet corn, and cornbread mix for a moist texture. Cheddar adds richness and a little saltiness.

review.reviewBody: I changed the recipe for the kids and it turned out that everyone really loved it. I left out the cheese, I added a pinch of kosher salt, 1 tablespoon of sugar and added extra butter about 1/4 cup, I really didn't measure, I baked it in a buttered 9x13 cake pan for 40 to 45 minutes, I needed the oven for the rest of the dinner so I took it out about 2 hours, maybe even longer, before we ate and just set it on the counter the warm temperature was perfect so I love the fact that I was able to use the oven for other dishes and it also free up my time since I was busy preparing a large meal. It was a winner and since I try so many new recipes the family asked me to keep this one as a regular, it pleased every palate.

Very good. I use all the ingredients except cheese and I only add 6 TBSP butter. We are savory taste lovers so I add 1/8Tsp ground nutmeg. I drain the whole kernel corn. Sometimes I use frozen corn. I have also made this with GREEK 2% yogurt - plain no flavor. 

Now - I beat the eggs then add the sour cream and combine WELL with the eggs. Then I add the corn & nutmeg and combine WELL with the eggs & sour cream . Then I add corn muffin mix and mix well. Only then -LAST- I add butter and mix well. It goes into a 1-1/2 quart casserole dish. Because the dish is deep it takes 1+ hour to bake at 350°F. We don't like soupy corn casserole and -- my oven IS NOT calibrated correctly so your cooking time might be more or less.

Rave reviews and super easy. I had the Penguin cornbread mix from Costco and was worried the measurements would be off. But not at all. I used 1/2 of the cornbread mix bag and baked it on a 9x13 glass dish for 55 minutes. I also mixed in the shredded cheese before baking. The consistency was perfect.

I have made this several times, for family and friends, and everyone loves it! First time, I made it as written--- GREAT! But I didn't have the correct size baking pan, so I used one that was slightly larger. When it was brown on top, I tested the inside with a toothpick, and it was done. Another time, I added diced red pepper, diced onion, a 4 oz. can of diced green chilis and a 4 oz. can of sliced black olives (be sure you drain the chilis and olives!). This was also great! Once I used half and half instead of sour cream, since I didn't have sour cream, and it also came out great! In my opinion, it is very rich and filling, and I have always gotten 8-12 servings from this recipe, serving it as a side dish. Maybe if it's served as a main dish, it is only 4 servings?

I change the recipe a bit; I didn’t have enough sour cream so I used Brown Cow brand’s Maple Yogurt instead. Then guess what! It was a great surprise! The aroma of maple syrup from yogurt and cornbread was so tempting I kept checking my oven ... which lead to my fall of final product to be a bit of visual failure! Yikes! It looked very picturesque when it first came out of the oven - full bodied casserole. As you can see, the center is bit carved in. It sank as it cooled off. I think it’s because I kept opening the oven because I was emotionally weak to fight off such a wonderful smell in my kitchen. So don’t do what I did, cheers! It was big hit at my social distancing 6’ apart dinner.

I made it for Thanksgiving dinner and everyone loved it. I altered it very slightly by only doing 1/2 C. Sour Cream and 1/2 Cup of Cream Cheese. It came out moist but not soupy, which how we prefer our Corn bread Casserole. It looked beautiful when cut. I only wish, I would have taken a picture of it after it was cut to show how pretty it presented. I also doubled the recipe so that it would make a 9 X 11 pan.

I doubled the recipe (so I also added a little more baking time to it) and added a little more cheddar cheese to it and it came out wonderfully. I use this for mainly holidays, and the family keeps asking about it.

I took this as a side dish to a Thanksgiving dinner. Rave reviews!! It was a hit. I couldn't find an 11 oz can of corn so I used a larger size and just cooked it about 10 minutes longer and added about 10 min. when the cheese was added. Turned out beautifully.
This is a great and simple recipe. I left out the cheese and doubled the recipe. Cooked at 375 for 1.5 hours in 9x13 pan. Came out perfect for Thanksgiving dinner.

This recipe is almost like the recipe that I had growing up. I have modified it to make it a little more healthy. I only use 3 Tbs of butter, skip the cheese, and I use 1 16oz bag of frozen corn instead of the whole canned corn. I like it to be a higher percentage of corn and less bread. Also, you can cook this in the crockpot 2 1/2 hours on high, stirring it after the first hour. Or, you can cook it in the microwave for 20 minutes on high, stirring it every 5 minutes (it doesn't get the golden brown top though). Thanks for sharing a wonderful recipe. People always ask for the recipe when I take it to parties.

I have been making this recipe for over 5yrs--I have doubled the recipe because it is so popular and I wanted to have some left overs. I use fat free or low fat sour cream. I do not use an egg--I just mix everything together and place in greased or pam sprayed large casserole dish--350 for 45 min and then add shredded cheddar cheese sprinkle on the top & cook 15min more--
it should be moist inside--not too dry---this recipe can be part of a Mexican meal--so substitute cheddar cheese with pepper jack shredded cheese--

This is a requirement in our family. My daughter works for a firm and she is required to bring this dish’s along with deviled eggs to their work party every year. She can’t come if she doesn’t have this dish with her and the bowl is clean when everyone is done.
Hands-down, this is THE side dish everyone asks me to bring to holiday gatherings! Easy and delicious, sweet and savory at the same time. LOVE!
I have to make a double batch every Thanksgiving and there is never any leftovers!!

I made this recipe as written using a gluten free cornbread mix. Corn casserole is a family favorite around my house and I was interested in how my family would like this one. They could tell there was something different with this recipe (mainly the eggs) and it was not the corn casserole I normally make. They liked it, said it was okay but prefer the recipe I usually make. They rated it a 4.
Love this, for Thanksgiving and when I have a strong corn craving.

It was delicious! I made it for 16 servings for 6 people. I used Monterey Jack, Sharp Cheddar and Provolone cheese. It was practically finished the same day. Everyone loved it, and I'm glad that I increased the recipe. I'm looking forward to making this dish again. Thank you!
